findings.claim: The gate authorization callback can reject administering-entity resolve and command-lookup routes for callers that have `resolve_administering_entity` but not case-write authority, violating the route capability contract.
findings.evidence: Acceptance 1.4 says the authorization callback checks `case:read` or `resolve_administering_entity`; in the `PolicyTarget::Resolution { case_id, write }` branch the code first sets `required` to `resolve_administering_entity` for writes, but then for every write route calls `state.services.authorize_case_write_target(&context, &capabilities, case_id)` before allowing the request, tying resolve/lookup authorization to the case-write target path rather than the resolver capability.
findings.suggested_fix: Add/use a case-target authorization method that verifies tenant visibility of the case under the already-selected resolver/read capability without requiring case-write authority, and use it for `administering-entity` POST and command lookup.
